name: Verapamil scar gel

lead:
Verapamil is a calcium channel blocker long used for blood pressure, angina and heart rhythm. Researchers have looked at it for scars because it has been reported to act on the fibroblast cells that lay down scar tissue, with the aim of producing flatter, less visible scars and keloids.
Most scar work uses verapamil injected into the lesion by a clinician, in comparison with steroid injections. Topical use has been tested in smaller studies, such as one in which five observers judged photographs of 120 patients three months after abdominoplasty.

paras: In the clinical studies, verapamil is applied or injected under medical supervision, usually on keloids or on fresh surgical scars. Topical gels are generally compounded preparations rather than packaged cosmetic products. No dosing or preparation instructions are given here.

Verapamil taken by mouth commonly causes constipation, dizziness, low blood pressure and headache, and less often slow heart rate or heart block. Topical scar use is off-label, and people on heart medication or with heart rhythm problems are usually advised to discuss any use with a clinician.

angle.text: People interested in scar improvement look at verapamil as a way to reduce raised scars and keloids. Most of the supporting work involves clinician-given injections; topical use has been examined in a smaller number of studies.

lead: Verapamil scar gel refers to topical preparations of verapamil, a calcium channel blocker approved in the United States in 1981 for heart conditions, used in an experimental way to improve the look of scars. [1]

The appearance goal is a scar that is flatter, softer and less raised or discolored. A 2014 study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery had a panel of five observers (a plastic surgeon, dermatologist, physiotherapist, biologist and a layperson) assess photographs of 120 abdominoplasty patients three months after surgery to evaluate topical verapamil as a modulator of healing. [2]
Clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov compare verapamil injected into keloids with triamcinolone, the standard steroid injection. [3][4]

paras: Verapamil is approved for hypertension, angina and supraventricular tachycardia, and is also used for migraine and cluster headache prevention. A topical form has been used for plantar fibromatosis, a fibrous tissue disorder, with tentative evidence. [1]
In scar care it has been investigated for keloids, which are raised scars that grow beyond the original wound, and for the prevention of scarring after surgery. [2][3][4]
The 2014 abdominoplasty study evaluated topical verapamil as a modulator of the healing process using photographs assessed by five observers of 120 patients at three months. [2]

Two registered trials compare intralesional triamcinolone acetonide with intralesional verapamil hydrochloride in 60 patients each: one completed in 2025 and one with a Phase 4 design not yet recruiting at registration. [3][4] Results from these registrations are not summarized here.

When taken by mouth, verapamil commonly causes constipation (about 7%), dizziness, nausea, low blood pressure and headache; less commonly it causes edema, slow heart rate, heart block, rash, flushing and raised liver enzymes. Gum enlargement is also reported. [1]
Overdose can cause weakness, slow heart rate, low blood pressure and abnormal rhythms. [1] How much of the drug is absorbed through the skin from a gel is not established.

Verapamil gel is not a standard cosmetic product. It appears mainly in clinical research and in compounded prescriptions from physicians who treat keloids and surgical scars. Established scar options such as silicone gel sheeting, pressure therapy, steroid injections and laser are described in dermatology references on keloid treatment. [5]

timeline.event: Verapamil is approved for medical use in the United States as a cardiovascular drug. [1]
Aesthetic Plastic Surgery publishes a study of topical verapamil as a scar modulator after abdominoplasty. [2]
Trials comparing intralesional verapamil with triamcinolone for keloids are registered. [3][4]
